rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi links this scene to 39:69 and identifies the angels around the Throne as its bearers and other near angels, as confirmed by 40:7.
rows.anchor: Contextual indication shows that this verse is adjacent to verse sixty nine and the angels mentioned are the ones which carry the throne of the Almighty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene warns idolaters who rely on angels for intercession: even the throne-bearing angels will be occupied with fear and glorifying God, leaving lesser angels still less able to intercede.
rows.anchor: because of the horror of that day they too would be very anxious and gathered around the throne of the Almighty busy extolling Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment will decide everyone's case with complete justice and truth, leaving no opportunity or courage for anyone to intervene or intercede.
rows.anchor: the cases of people will be decided with complete justice and truth; neither will there be any opportunity for anyone to intervene

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once God's perfect mercy and justice appear, believers praise Him and the angels around the Throne join them.
rows.anchor: The believers will chant this cry and the angels of the throne will also join the believers in this chanting

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deserves praise because He establishes justice and distinguishes truth from falsehood; without judgment, evil would prevail unaccountably and the Creator would not merit praise.
rows.anchor: what makes God worthy of praise and gratitude is His justice and His discernment of truth and falsehood

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perfect mercy and justice on Judgment Day will dispel everyone's anxiety and doubt, make the universe resound with praise, and bring the awaited dawn of praise in a world radiant with God's light.
rows.anchor: When on the Day of Judgement the perfect mercy and perfect justice manifest themselves, then the anxiety and doubt of everyone will be appeased

none: verse text, translation and publication notice only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥā Mīm names this sūrah; Islahi says the remaining Makkan sūrahs in this group share that name and the same mood, with abbreviated letters discussed at the beginning of al-Baqarah.
rows.anchor: this sūrah and all the remaining Makkan sūrahs of in this group share this name and the mood of each one of them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the Book's revelation from the Mighty, All-Knowing God is both a favor and a warning: its careful arrangement calls people to value it, seek guidance, and give thanks.
rows.anchor: portray a favour as well as sound an admonition to the opponents of the Qur’ān

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's might means He controls everything and can punish opponents of the Qur’an in this life and the next, with no one able to stop Him.
rows.anchor: Since He is Mighty, He has power and control over everything; He can give all kinds of punishment both in this world and in the next

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As All-Knowing, God understands the conflict caused by the Book, how its bearers are treated, opponents' intentions, and when those intentions must be stopped.
rows.anchor: He fully knows which phase is the tussle that has ensued because of the elaborate revelation of this Book

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ṭawl can mean blessing, self-sufficiency, might, or gift; Islahi prefers might because the verse uses a contrasting style.
rows.anchor: means “blessing, self-sufficience, might and gift.” I have preferred the meaning of “might” keeping in view the contrasting style found in the verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has both forgiving and punitive attributes and authority, so a person may accept the Book and hope for mercy or oppose it and await punishment.
rows.anchor: God has both these types of attributes and vested in Him are both types of authority

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God is worthy of worship; all people return to Him for judgment, and no one else receives their return or intercedes without His permission.
rows.anchor: No once except God is worthy of worship. On the Day of Judgement, everyone shall return to Him, and all their matters shall be decided by Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs of God are the revealed verses mentioned in 40:2; calling them God's signs emphasizes their force as conclusive evidence.
rows.anchor: refers to the verses of the Book whose revelation is referred to in verse two

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are those who rejected the punishment warned of by the Qur’an; messengers' warnings were dismissed as bluffs because worldly success led people to reject and mock them.
rows.anchor: when the messengers of God warned them of God’s punishment they regarded it to be a bluff and on the basis of their worldly successes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and Muslims are assured that those frivolously opposing the Qur’an have rejected its punishment warnings; arrogance and present prosperity make them mock, though past nations were seized at their height.
rows.anchor: This verse refers to this aspect. It assures the Prophet (sws) and through him the Muslims that the frivolous talk people are engaging in

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the warning apparently addresses the Prophet, its rebuke targets Quraysh opponents proud of their power, who questioned why and how punishment could reach them.
rows.anchor: the rebuke and anger found in them is directed at the rejecters of the Quraysh who

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rendered as “O” means free movement; the occasion may also convey arrogance or conceit, which Islahi tried to retain.
rows.anchor: The word O means “walking about and coming and going freely.” Occasion can also incorporate the meaning of arrogance and conceit in it
